game1.summary: The Brewers held off a ninth-inning Rays rally to win Game 1, 3-2, at the first World Series game in Milwaukee since 1982. Jackson Chourio opened the first with a single, Christian Yelich drove him in with a triple in his first-ever World Series at-bat, and William Contreras singled home Yelich for a 2-0 lead. Tampa Bay got a run back in the fourth after a Junior Caminero double, and Chourio's two-out single in the seventh brought home Cooper Pratt for a 3-1 cushion. In the ninth the Rays loaded the bases against Trevor Megill, and what looked like a game-ending double play was overturned on replay, which let a run score. Megill then struck out Jonny DeLuca with the tying run on third to end it. Jacob Misiorowski set the tone with a 103.5 mph first pitch, the fastest ever recorded in a World Series.

key_moments: 1st: Chourio leadoff single, Yelich RBI triple (his first World Series at-bat), Contreras RBI single for 2-0.
Misiorowski's first pitch was clocked at 103.5 mph, a World Series record.
4th: Caminero's 112.7 mph double set up the Rays' first run, scored on a Liam Hicks groundout (2-1).
5th and 6th: Contreras threw out Victor Mesa Jr. trying to take third, then caught Jonathan Aranda stealing second.
7th: Pratt walked and scored on Chourio's two-out single (3-1).
9th: bases loaded, an apparent game-ending double play was reversed on review (Pratt's foot was off the bag) and a run scored (3-2). Megill struck out DeLuca to finish it.
No home runs by either team. Robin Yount threw the ceremonial first pitch wearing Bob Uecker's sport coat.
